name: Chandrayaan-2
payload: 3850 kg launch mass; 2379 kg orbiter; 1471 kg Vikram lander including the 27 kg Pragyan rover
first: India's first attempt at a soft landing on the Moon
description: Chandrayaan-2 was ISRO's second Moon mission and its first attempt at a soft landing: an orbiter, the Vikram lander and the 27 kg Pragyan rover, launched together from Sriharikota on 2019-07-22. The orbiter was captured into lunar orbit on 2019-08-20, Vikram separated on 2019-09-02, and the lander began its powered descent toward the south polar region on 2019-09-06. Contact was lost at about 2.1 km altitude and Vikram crashed; a failure analysis committee attributed the loss to a combination of factors, including a software error in the descent guidance and control. NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter later found the impact site at 70.881° S, 22.784° E, after a volunteer from Chennai spotted debris in its images. The orbiter kept working: its eight instruments (CLASS, XSM, DFSAR, IIRS, ChACE-2, TMC-2, RAMBHA-DFRS and OHRC) were still mapping the Moon from polar orbit in 2026, and its OHRC camera later imaged the Chandrayaan-3 landing site.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: LVM3 M1 (formerly GSLV Mk III) from Sriharikota 2019-07-22.

events.label: TLI
events.note: Trans-lunar injection 2019-08-13, after a series of Earth-orbit raising burns.

events.label: LOI
events.note: Lunar orbit insertion 2019-08-20 into an 18,072 x 114 km orbit.

events.label: VIKRAM SEPARATION
events.note: Vikram, with the Pragyan rover inside, separates from the orbiter 2019-09-02.

events.label: LANDER LOST
events.note: Powered descent begins about 20:08 UTC on 2019-09-06 (7 September in India); contact is lost at about 2.1 km altitude and Vikram crashes.

events.label: CRASH SITE FOUND
events.note: NASA's LRO locates Vikram's impact site at 70.881° S, 22.784° E, announced 2019-12-02; the orbiter keeps mapping.
